abstract: Background: The transcription factor TFEB/HLH-30 is a well-established regulator of autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis during starvation and stress, and it plays important roles in development and homeostasis. Our previous work demonstrated that Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30 also functions under basal physiological conditions in mature neurons, where it promotes the expansion of endo-lysosomal degradative capacity during early adulthood. These findings raised the question of whether HLH-30 promotes lysosomal gene expression more broadly during early adulthood, and, more generally, whether its basal transcriptional functions depend on animal age. To address these questions, we analyzed the impact of hlh-30 loss on the transcriptome at two larval stages, L1 and L4, and two adult ages, Day 3 and Day 6, in hermaphrodites grown under basal conditions. Results: We identified modest effects of hlh-30 loss on the transcriptome that varied by stage/age. Enrichment analyses of genes downregulated in hlh-30 mutants identified functions related to defense response at L1 and in adulthood, and to cuticle development in adulthood. On the other hand, a role for hlh-30 in the basal expression of autophagy genes was exclusively detected in L1 larvae. A subset of genes encoding cathepsins showed decreased expression in the adult hlh-30 mutant; however, our results indicate that HLH-30 is not broadly required for basal expression of most lysosome biogenesis genes in adulthood. We also detected a trend toward reduced expression of genes involved in germline function at the L4 stage, when spermatogenesis occurs, and found that loss of hlh-30 resulted in reduced sperm and progeny numbers. In addition, we found that hlh-30 is required for full progeny survival through larval development. Finally, we identified a gene with increased expression at all four stages in the hlh-30 mutant, the germline transcription factor-encoding ztf-28. Knockdown of ztf-28 partially suppressed the reductions in progeny number and survival, suggesting that its increased expression contributes to these phenotypes. Conclusions: This study reveals roles for HLH-30 in transcriptome regulation under basal growth conditions that vary in both magnitude and content by animal age. Further, it demonstrates a previously unappreciated requirement for HLH-30 in promoting progeny number and survival, broadening our understanding of the physiological roles of this conserved transcription factor.

metadata.title: Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30/TFEB has age-dependent effects on the transcriptome and is required for normal progeny number and larval survival under basal growth conditions

summary: C. elegans HLH-30/TFEB loss alters basal transcriptome in stage- and age-dependent ways, reduces sperm and progeny numbers, and impairs larval survival.
title: Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30/TFEB has age-dependent effects on the transcriptome and is required for normal progeny number and larval survival under basal growth conditions
